subject: RSW_Mynock

reply.subject: RSW_Mynock

observed.facings.png: Three facings at one scale. South: a creature seen face-on with the head at the bottom. It has two bulging dark eyes on top of a round open sucker mouth ringed with bristles. Short broad wings with claw tips spread left and right, and a spiked tail points straight up behind the body. East: a side profile flying right. It has two large ragged, finger-ribbed membrane wings raised, a long thin tail ending in a spade, small clawed hind legs, and a sucker mouth with bulging eyes at the front. North: the back view, with a ribbed back, two small knobs at the shoulders, wings spread (the left one larger and raised), hind legs, and a long tail with a spade curving down-left. No face. The hide is brown to olive with reddish mottling and reads as painterly.
observed.south.png: South static at full resolution: the face toward the camera, with the sucker disc, bristles and two eyes. The wings are spread to the sides and the tail points up. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: East static: a side profile with both wings up, ragged edges between the ribs, the tail trailing left, clawed feet under the body, and the sucker mouth facing right. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: North static: the rear, with back, shoulder knobs, wings, legs and tail. No eyes or mouth. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the mynock is roughly a third of the human's height and sits inside one cell. In normal play (32 px/cell) it is a small speckled mark beside the human and the rat, still faintly readable as a winged shape.
observed.flight_1.png: East frame 1: wings raised high, the static's upstroke pose.
observed.flight_2.png: East frame 2: wings slightly lower and a little compressed. The body is unchanged.
observed.flight_3.png: East frame 3: wings at mid-beat, flattened vertically about the shoulder.
observed.flight_4.png: East frame 4: wings squashed nearly flat into a thin band at the shoulder. The membrane texture is compressed but intact. The body is unchanged.
observed.flight_5.png: East frame 5: the flattest pose, both wings a thin horizontal sliver. Ragged edges are still visible. The body, tail and head are unchanged.
observed.flight_6.png: East frame 6: matches frame 4 (the return stroke).
observed.flight_8.png: East frame 8: matches frame 2. The cycle ping-pongs back to frame 1.
observed.flight_9.png: North frame 1: wings narrower and more upright than the static, turned about the shoulders. The body is unchanged.
observed.flight_10.png: North frame 2: wings a little more spread.
observed.flight_11.png: North frame 3: matches the static's spread pose.
observed.flight_12.png: North frame 4: wings lowered and foreshortened, tips dropping toward horizontal.
observed.flight_13.png: North frame 5: wings at the lowest, most foreshortened pose. The roots stay attached at the shoulders with no visible seam.
observed.flight_17.png: South frame 1: wings tilted up and slightly shortened about the shoulders. The face, body and tail are unchanged.
observed.flight_18.png: South frame 2: wings raised a little more.
observed.flight_19.png: South frame 3: matches the static's spread.
observed.flight_20.png: South frame 4: wings angled down and foreshortened.
observed.flight_21.png: South frame 5: wings at the lowest, shortest pose, still attached at the shoulders with claw tips intact.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the sucker-disc face and both eyes toward the camera in the static and in all 8 south frames.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows the back, shoulder knobs and tail, with no face or eyes, in the static and in all 8 north frames.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: The owner approved these statics. The flip-book only moves the wings and adds no overhead view. South has a steep camera angle with the tail rising behind, but it is not a rotated top-down view.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured 20% height spread comes from pose: the south tail sticks straight up, while the east body is long and low. The body plate is identical within each direction's frames, so the beat adds no size jump.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same mottled brown-olive hide, sucker mouth, spade tail and ribbed wings appear in every facing. The body is pixel-identical across frames within each direction.

SIGNATURE.seen: Broad leathery wings, the whip tail with its spade and the bristled sucker mouth are legible on south and east.

CANON.seen: Bat layout with finger-ribbed membrane wings, clawed hind legs and a spade-tipped whip tail. Round bristled sucker with bulging eyes. Ragged wing edges. Wrinkled painterly hide. No snout, and it is not a bird or a dragon.

STYLE.seen: Painterly, realistic and wrinkled, with no heavy keylines. The bulging eyes are glossy but sit on a grotesque sucker face, so it is not cute.

OURS.seen: The owner-approved own statics; the flip-book is cut from them.

ALPHA.seen: Every frame sits on clean transparency, with no shadow or backdrop.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The body plate is identical in every frame and only the wings beat: turned and foreshortened about the shoulder on south and north, squashed vertically on east. No tears, fragments or seams at the wing roots, and no identity drift. Each direction ping-pongs through 5 distinct poses, and the beat reads.

SCALE.seen: About a third of the human's height, which fits 'small parasite' at drawSize 0.6.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell it is a small speckled winged shape. It is faint but separate from the ground.

WINGS_FOLDED.seen: This candidate is the flight flip-book. The grounded statics with spread wings are owner-approved art, and raised wings are polish by the module rule.
